National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
352 AM EDT Sun Oct 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Coastal Flood Advisories were added, with the other hazards
maintained as is. Continue to monitor the need for expansion of
the Flood Watch.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Remnants of Isaias bring rain, breezy conditions, and
  potential for tornadoes today.

- 2) Above normal temperatures through mid week, then cooler
  conditions as moisture starved fronts move through.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Remnants of Isaias bring rain, breezy conditions, 
and potential for tornadoes today.

Rain associated with the remnants of Hurricane Isaias has overspread 
the entire region early this morning. Observations indicate most of 
this is light, though a few pockets of moderate rain have been 
reported in Central VA. A few stations along the central VA Blue 
Ridge have already measured over 1" of rain, with most of Central VA 
at or just above half an inch. Winds have also started picking up in 
the Alleghenies, with the strongest gust at 43mph in Garrett County. 

Synoptically not much has changed as the remnant mid-level 
circulation of Isaias is now a large cutoff low over the TN Valley. 
Forcing for ascent over the Mid-Atlantic is helping increase the 
coverage of rain. The interaction of the cutoff low to the west and 
surface high to the east will create a large area of convergence 
/ broad frontal zone over the Mid-Atlantic. SPC Mesoanalysis 
indicates that PWATs of 2" are surging north into our area from NC 
and southern VA.

Rain totals are generally still around 1.5-2.5" across the area. 
Orographic effects of easterly winds into the Blue Ridge will result 
in 3-4" of rain along the eastern slopes into the Piedmont. The 
Flood Watch in effect for those areas continues. Some of the high 
res models indicate the potential for enhanced rainfall over the DC 
metro late this evening as a surface wave of low pressure approaches 
then slows right around DC, before quickly departing to the east 
late tonight. Any additional rain in the metro area could certainly 
lead to flooding concerns, so will continue to monitor model and 
radar trends to see if the Flood Watch need to be expanded. 

In terms of the severe weather threat, SPC has expanded the Slight 
Risk into most of Central VA, with a Marginal up into the I-81 
corridor to the MD/PA border. Once the main shield of rain departs 
to the north this afternoon, most of the area enters a brief lull 
where we could see some breaks in the clouds. There's a better 
chance for this to occur over Central VA to Southern MD. A wave of 
surface low pressure then tracks through the area this afternoon. If 
this can take advantage of any present instability, there is more 
than enough shear to fuel organized severe convection. Model 
soundings still show elongated hodographs, so the tornado threat is 
going to be front and center, though damaging wind gusts are also 
possible. The biggest question mark remains how much instability can 
develop, and how far north that instability will reach. Right now, 
it appears the most favorable area is going to be east of the Blue 
Ridge and south of Route 50. 

The Wind Advisory remains through late this morning for the 
Alleghenies and Blue Ridge where gusts of 45-50 mph are expected. 
Elsewhere, breezy conditions develop late this morning into the 
afternoon, with the strongest gusts around 20-30 mph. 

Another round of steady rain is likely tonight as the cutoff low 
aloft moves across the Mid-Atlantic. Precip comes to an end from 
west to east Monday morning as the remnants of Isaias finally push 
offshore. Humid and warm conditions for Monday afternoon, though 
most of the area is going to be dry.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Above normal temperatures through mid week, then
cooler conditions as moisture starved fronts move through.

Brief ridging may bring high temperatures Tuesday and Wednesday
to near 80 degrees. Low pressure passing north of the area will
send a cold front southward sometime on Wednesday. Most of the 
rain likely remains across Pennsylvania, although some showers 
may sneak southward. 

There remains significant model spread the progression of
additional fronts and upper troughs at the end of this week into
next weekend. However, the trend remains for cooler conditions
as highs return closer to normal values for Thursday and
Friday. 

&&

.AVIATION /07Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Conditions are deteriorating as a steady rain moves into the region. 
IFR conditions are expected at all terminals by late morning, and 
remain that way through tonight. It is possible some breaks in the 
clouds occur this afternoon, but they build back in this evening. 
Guidance is indicating the potential for LIFR CIGs late this 
evening. Conditions begin to quickly improve tonight as northwest 
winds take hold, with VFR conditions returning Monday morning. 

Northwest winds gust around 20-25 knots Monday afternoon, then 
diminish Monday night into Tuesday. Prevailing VFR conditions 
are anticipated from Tuesday through Thursday. Passing showers 
Thursday night into Friday could bring brief sub-VFR conditions.

&&

.MARINE...
SCA conditions expected to continue through tonight as the remnants 
of Isaias move across the region. Winds gust around 30 knots at 
times throughout the day, and some gusts to Gale force are possible. 
It is becoming unlikely we see sustained Gale conditions, thus the 
Gale Warning is likely to be dropped for the central bay in the next 
couple of hours. 

Clusters of thunderstorms are likely to move across parts of the 
waters this afternoon. It is possible that Special Marine Warnings 
may be needed for wind gusts in excess of 35-40 knots and possible 
waterspouts.

Winds over the waters diminish late tonight, but will pick back up 
Monday afternoon. Another round of SCAs is going to be needed to 
account for these northwest winds. Winds drop again Monday night.
Winds could fluctuate in & out of SCA criteria between Wednesday
and Thursday as a cold front passes through.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Increasing onshore winds and elevated tide levels due to the New 
Moon will result in coastal flooding during the high tide this 
afternoon to evening. Coastal Flood Advisories have been issued for 
some locations, and it is possible additional ones need to be 
issued. For Annapolis, it is going to be close as to whether it 
reaches Moderate flood, so have maintained the Coastal Flood Watch 
for now. Water levels quickly decrease Monday morning as offshore 
winds follow.
